headline: Drossel-Schwabl forest fire (cellular automaton / SOC): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; fitted tau=1.199 (kmin=1), nonzero fire sizes span 4.2 decades (max/median=363x), stationary tree density 0.349/0.337 (empty/trees inits)

verdicts.gate: P1 fitted tail exponent tau in [1.0, 2.5] (power-law fire sizes, SOC)
P2 heavy-tailed: nonzero fire sizes span >= 2.0 decades AND max >= 100.0x median nonzero
P3 stationary tree density init-independent (|empty - trees| <= 0.05)

extra.fit_method: exact discrete power-law MLE (zeta-likelihood; Clauset et al. 2009), kmin=1
extra.implementation: standard double-separation (instantaneous burning); fire size = toroidal connected von-Neumann cluster size of the struck tree
extra.model_class: cellular automaton / self-organized criticality (NOT agent-stepping ABM): synchronous local update rules on a grid of cells; there are no agents, no scheduler, no per-agent decisions
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic CA/SOC result; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the SOC fire-size power-law and would catch an artifact (a non-power-law distribution or an init-dependent density)
extra.caveat: the forest-fire model is only APPROXIMATELY scale-free: the fire-size distribution has known deviations from a pure power law at the largest sizes (a bump / finite-size cutoff), and the precise exponent is debated in the literature; the fitted tau is reported with its kmin and across a range of kmin (results.json tau_by_kmin)

citations: Drossel, B. & Schwabl, F. (1992). Self-organized critical forest-fire model. Phys. Rev. Lett. 69:1629-1632. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.1629.

Grassberger, P. (2002). Critical behaviour of the Drossel-Schwabl forest fire model. New J. Phys. 4:17 (the forest-fire model is only approximately scale-free; large-size deviations and the debated exponent).
Clauset, A., Shalizi, C.R. & Newman, M.E.J. (2009). Power-law distributions in empirical data. SIAM Review 51(4):661-703 (discrete-MLE estimator).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction. The literature anchor for P1 is a power-law fire-size distribution; the exact exponent is debated, so the locked window [1.0, 2.5] is deliberately broad.
